adminfiles: The PO area of admin-guides is thin on pages and thick on prose: 100 files match the PO filename sweep (230,201 bytes) and 127 files contain "purchase order", but the corpus names exactly TWO surfaces reached by their own click path off Administration > Invoice — Purchase Order Matching Rules and Purchase Order Configuration. Everything else is a section on a page already in the graph, an end-user/processor screen under the Requests menu, or a file specification with no screen: Purchase Order Import is an FTP/web-service job plus a record-layout spec with zero click paths, and the PR and PO Processor is a back-office processing tool reached from Requests, not Administration. rolesmenus: Entering from roles, permissions and feature activation, the PO admin-configuration surface that the corpus actually names — and that is not already one of the 18 built pages — is only TWO pages: Purchase Order Matching Rules and Purchase Order Configuration. Both have their own Administration > Invoice left-menu click path and both are gated exclusively to the Invoice Configuration administrator, the PO Matching Rules gate stated twice (once per guide directory). A corpus-wide census of every "Administration > Invoice > X" string returns 23 distinct labels of which exactly two are PO-domain, so Group 3 is genuinely thin; everything else the PO area configures resolves to Policies, Invoice Settings, Forms and Fields, Company Locations, Workflows (its own group), the shared User Permissions page, or an end-user screen with no config of its own.

roster.headline: Group 3 is TWO pages, not eleven — Purchase Order Matching Rules and Purchase Order Configuration. All six sweeps, entering from six directions, converged on the same two surfaces, and four exhaustive censuses I ran myself confirm it: of 39 documented `Invoice > X` targets only two are PO-domain; of 27 `(left menu)` labels only one is; of 80 `The X page appears` sentences only one is; and of the ten PO-domain `The X window appears` sentences nine are end-user dialogs. I settled the two real kind-disagreements — "Purchase Order Matching Set" is an ALIAS SAP uses loosely for the same surface (the decisive evidence sits inside one topic that says you are already "in Purchase Order Matching Set" before Edit "opens" it), and Purchase Order Settings / Purchase Request Settings belong to Workflows > Settings tab, not Invoice Settings, proven by the built Invoice Settings roster returning grep -c 0 on their lead setting. I also removed four bad seeds the sweeps proposed: two Audit Rules topics mis-filed under PO Matching Rules, and one Workflows setting plus one end-user topic mis-filed under PO Configuration.

pages.identityNotes:
PAGE-HOOD, SETTLED. It is the only PO label in the entire corpus that appears with '(left menu)' (I harvested all 27 such labels), the only PO surface named in a 'The X page appears' arrival sentence (I harvested all 80), and it has its own list grid: 'Each rule set appears in a row that includes the following columns:' with Rule Set Name / In Use / Associated Policies (access-...-8407c500.md). Its exclusive role gate is stated TWICE, once per guide directory. It is not one of the 18 built pages — the PO Matching Ruleset control on Policies is a pointer INTO this page's rule sets, not this page.

ONE PAGE, NOT FOUR. The access-/create-/edit-/copy- topic family is one page with four buttons: copy-purchase-order-matching-rules-c6d4106a.md redirects wholesale to Step 1, and edit- operates on a selected row of the same list. This is the AUDIT RULES precedent (one page, tabs and buttons), not the Forms-and-Fields precedent. DO NOT SPLIT. Three-Way Matching and Receipt Confirmation are likewise not pages: both are configured here ('Receipt confirmation is part of the PO Matching feature set.' — overview-8b37481c.md).

THE 'PURCHASE ORDER MATCHING SET' DISPUTE — RESOLVED. The sweeps disagreed on kind: clickpaths called it 'unclear'; adminfiles, toolsguides, graphrefs and setupflow called it a dialog. I settled it in the corpus. The decisive evidence sits inside ONE topic, edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md, whose two consecutive steps read 'In Purchase Order Matching Set, select the rule set row under Rule Set Name.' and then 'Click Edit to open Purchase Order Matching Set.' — you are already IN the surface before Edit OPENS it. Meanwhile access-...-8407c500.md places that identical row-and-column list on 'the Purchase Order Matching Rules page', and step-1-...-4d3866f3.md places the identical Copy action 'In Purchase Order Matching Rules'. VERDICT: 'Purchase Order Matching Set' is an ALIAS SAP uses loosely for this same surface, not a distinct page — the Validation-Rules-under-Audit-Rules precedent. Carried as an alias so a Chromium driver has the string.

CONTRADICTION PRESERVED, NOT RECONCILED: the editor stack is named FOUR ways in the same 2026_08 corpus — 'Purchase Order Matching Set' (edit-604d1e31, step-3), 'Purchase Order Matching Rules' (the list page's own string, used for the editor in step-2: 'In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name.'), 'Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window' (configure-three-way-matching), and 'Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions' (step-4). The automation needs all four.

DOCUMENTED CLICK TREE: page (list) -> select rule set + Edit -> 'Purchase Order Matching Set' (edit mode/dialog, carries the Rule Groups list) -> Edit Rules -> 'Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window' (Name, Rules tab, Life to Date tab, Level, Payment Request, Purchase Order, Tolerance, Exception Message, Allow Submit/Approve). Side branches: named rule group + Add -> 'Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions'; Rule Set or rule condition + Edit Confirmation -> 'Select Confirmation Type' window.

STRUCTURAL CONTRADICTION TO PRESERVE — THE MIDDLE NAV NODE. Every documented click path puts this page DIRECTLY under Administration > Invoice, never under 'Invoice Processing Admin'. I censused that node: 27 occurrences naming Policies, Workflows, Invoice Settings, Group Configurations, Forms and Fields, Routing Configuration, Exceptions, Expense Types, Change Log, Email Reminders and Peppol Configuration — and never once a PO page. I checked the single apparent PO hit and it is a false positive ('Receiving Exception Email Notifications' in receiving-exception-email-notifications-from-concur-invoice-28039049.md, which is about Peppol). Groups 1/2/5 built with the middle node in their navPath. GROUP 3 MUST RECORD THE LITERAL THREE-SEGMENT PATH AND NOT NORMALISE THE MIDDLE NODE IN. This may be a doc gap rather than a UI fact; say so, do not silently fix it.

DOCUMENTED GAP TO RECORD, NOT GUESS: the Payment Request and Purchase Order field lists on the Rules tab are described but never enumerated — 'As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order.' The build must mark them unenumerated.

NAME COLLISION WARNING FOR THE FIELD BUILD: 'Rules tab' also names a tab on the Email Reminders page. Bind by page, not by tab label. And the 'Condition Editor' referenced in step-5 is a THIRD distinct condition builder, separate from the Audit Rules Condition page (Group 2, built) and from the PR/PO Processor Query Builder. Do not merge the three.

MERGE CORRECTION — TWO BAD SEEDS REMOVED. Sweep clickpaths listed conditions-if-portion-of-the-if-then-statement-85743324.md (2,390 B) and exceptions-then-portion-of-the-if-then-statement-6a3d96b1.md (1,944 B) as key files here. They belong to page.audit-rules (Group 2, already built). Removed.

Unlike Audit Rules and Tax Administration, this page's material is procedural PROSE, so extraction is slow per field despite the byte count (~2,100 bytes per expected field).

It also never appears with '(left menu)' anywhere, unlike Matching Rules. That is the same lexical habit SAP applies to 'Vendor Manager tool' and 'Company Locations tool', both of which the graph already treats as pages. I record the corpus's own word rather than smoothing it; functionally it behaves as a page with its own menu entry.

THIS IS THE SWEEP-C SAVE, and it is worth flagging to the build. It surfaced in TOOLS-GUIDES FIRST (preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md). Its admin-guides anchor is a 1,179-byte stub, and its 5,956-byte content file configure-purchase-orders-8128725e.md NEVER NAMES A NAV PATH. 'Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration.' and 'Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default.' A Chromium driver MUST select a Group as step 0 before any field on this page can be set. There is a SECOND scope inside the page: 'Ensure that you have selected the correct policy in the Policy list.' governs the Fields to Appear on Purchase Orders picker.

CONTRADICTION PRESERVED, NOT RECONCILED: tool vs window (see uiVariantEvidence). A left-menu tool and a modal window are different things for an automation; both readings stand.

NAME COLLISION — THE FORMS-AND-FIELDS TRAP IN A NEW COSTUME. 'PO Configuration' denotes TWO structurally distinct surfaces in the same 2026_08 corpus: (a) THIS standalone tool, called 'PO Configuration' in tools-guides/preview-a-purchase-order-846396e1.md ('Administrators who configure purchase orders in PO Configuration'); and (b) a SECTION ON THE POLICIES PAGE — 'In the PO Configuration section of the page that appears, select the Enable Concur Receiving option.' reached by 'Select Administration > Invoice > Polices (left menu). The Policies page appears.' (configure-concur-receiving-1ececc23.md — note SAP's own 'Polices' misspelling, quoted verbatim, inside a live click step, so an automation matching on 'Policies' misses the documented path). Anyone building from a grep on 'PO Configuration' will conflate them. The existing graph's own note on field.policies.is-po-policy ('Selecting it reveals the PO Configuration options') is one letter away from this conflation. RECORD BOTH; DO NOT COLLAPSE.

roster.reconciliation:
The lost map recorded ELEVEN PO-matching pages. I land on TWO, and I am not padding to eleven.

WHY I TRUST TWO. Six independent sweeps entering from six different directions — navigation, admin-guides filenames, tools-guides, roles and menus, existing-graph forward references, and setup flow — produced the same two-page answer with no dissent on either page. On top of that I ran four exhaustive censuses myself rather than taking the sweeps on trust: (1) every "Invoice > X" destination in both guide directories yields 39 distinct targets of which exactly two are PO-domain; (2) every "(left menu)" click label yields 27 phrasings of which exactly one is PO-domain (Purchase Order Matching Rules — Purchase Order Configuration never appears with "(left menu)" at all); (3) every "The X page appears" arrival sentence yields 80 page names of which exactly one is PO-domain; (4) every "The X window appears" sentence yields 68 window names, of which ten are PO-domain and nine of those ten are end-user dialogs. Two supporting censuses agree: "X tool" yields 50+ tool names of which exactly one is PO-domain, and "X Admin" yields no Receiving Admin, no Purchasing Admin node and no PO Admin. There is no third PO surface reachable by a documented click in this corpus version.

Two honest hypotheses for the gap, offered as hypotheses because the map itself is gone and I cannot check either.

HYPOTHESIS A — the original counted the dialog stack and the borrowed sections as pages. Enumerate every named PO-area surface a pass without page-hood discipline would call a page and you get EXACTLY ELEVEN: (1) Purchase Order Matching Rules, (2) Purchase Order Matching Set, (3) Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window, (4) Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, (5) Select Confirmation Type, (6) Purchase Order Configuration, (7) PO Configuration section on Policies, (8) Purchase Request Configuration section on Policies, (9) Purchase Order Settings, (10) Purchase Request Settings, (11) Purchase Order Policy. The arithmetic fit is exact. Nine of those eleven fail page-hood for reasons quoted in the roster: five are dialogs or tabs with no independent click path, two are conditional sections on the already-built Policies page, and two are settings tables whose one shared control the corpus places on Workflows.

HYPOTHESIS B — the original counted setup-flow STOPS rather than PO-unique pages. The PR&PO Setup Guide's configuration section says outright that "each step uses tools familiar to any administrator of Concur Invoice (forms and fields, workflow, role assignment, etc.), with some PR-specific tools as noted" (configuration-of-purchase-requests-8b369a1e.md), and its sibling topics walk roughly eleven stops: feature enablement, User Permissions, Forms and Fields, the PR vendor form, Workflows plus Feature Hierarchies, Policies, Group Configurations, Company Locations, Shipping Configuration, Units Of Measure, Purchase Order Configuration, Exceptions. Only ONE of those is a page the graph does not already have.

Both hypotheses point the same way: the eleven counted SURFACES, not PAGES — most likely assembled before the "Forms and Fields is two pages / Audit Rules is one page" discipline existed. Two is what this corpus supports, and the delta is a finding about how the original was built.

ONE CAVEAT I WILL NOT PAPER OVER. This is a 2026_08 crawl. It is possible the original map was made against an earlier corpus that documented a surface SAP has since retired or merged. I found no positive evidence of that — no orphaned PO page label anywhere in either guide directory, and zero release-note hits for Purchase Order Matching Rules, Purchase Order Settings or Purchase Request Settings — but absence of evidence in a crawl is not proof, and a live-UI pass should be the tiebreaker.

Finally, the number that matters for planning is not 2. It is roughly 58 fields (about 40 on Purchase Order Matching Rules, about 18 on Purchase Order Configuration) across about 100 KB and 45 files. That is smaller than several single pages already in the graph — Audit Rules alone yielded 91 fields.
roster.splitProposal:
DO NOT SPLIT GROUP 3. Run it as a single pass.

The split rule exists to balance extraction cost across two runs and to stop two runs reading the same long catalog twice. Neither condition applies here.

1. SIZE. Two pages at three lenses each is roughly 6-8 agents, not the ~73 the eleven-page assumption implied. Estimated yield is ~58 fields across ~100 KB in 45 files — smaller than Audit Rules alone (91 fields). Splitting two pages into two halves would cost more orchestration overhead than it saves.

2. NO SHARED SOURCES TO PROTECT. The two pages share not one file. Purchase Order Matching Rules draws on 39 files / 84,820 bytes, all in the matching-and-confirmation family; Purchase Order Configuration draws on 6 files / 14,837 bytes, none of which appears in the other set. There is literally no long catalog that two halves would read twice, so the hazard the split rule guards against cannot occur.

3. ORDER WITHIN THE SINGLE RUN. Purchase Order Matching Rules FIRST — it is 5.7x the bytes, carries the group's entire contradiction load (the four-way editor naming, the Invoice Processing Admin middle-node absence, the unenumerated Payment Request / Purchase Order field lists), and its output (a rule set) is what the Policies dependency edge consumes. Purchase Order Configuration SECOND — small, dense, and one file does most of the work.

4. BUDGET EFFORT UNEVENLY, NOT PAGES. The cost asymmetry is in extraction difficulty, not page count. Purchase Order Matching Rules has rawTableFiles 0 and longCatalogs 0 — its largest enumeration anywhere is 7 entries and the material is procedural prose, so it is slow at roughly 2,100 bytes per expected field. Purchase Order Configuration is one clean 12-entry catalog with stated limits, roughly 800 bytes per field, and will come out fast. If a model-tier decision is needed: high-effort tier on Purchase Order Matching Rules, cheap tier on Purchase Order Configuration.

5. ONE THING TO ATTACH RATHER THAN SPLIT OUT. The Group 1 / Group 5 debt — policies-the-purchase-order-policy-new-experience-5a1ba7ef.md (15,800 B, the richest file in the PO area) and configure-forms-and-fields-for-purchase-order-copy-down-to-pr-f926eac7.md (10,109 B) — is PO-domain material Group 3's agents will have loaded anyway, but it writes onto page.policies and page.forms-and-fields. Either run it as a patch pass appended to Group 3 while the context is hot, or hand it back explicitly. What must NOT happen is letting it be mistaken for Group 3 pages, which is precisely how the roster inflates back toward eleven.

pagehood.verdict: TWO PAGES ENDORSED — no page added, none removed. I could not refute the page-hood of either entry and I attacked both from five directions. I re-ran the roster's three load-bearing censuses independently (30 `(left menu)` labels → 1 PO-domain; 79 `The X page appears` → 1 PO-domain; 48 `Invoice > X` destinations in both glyph forms → 2 PO-domain) and added a fourth the roster never ran: the built graph's own unresolved page references. Across 335 dependencies from four completed groups, the only PO-domain page names Groups 1/2/4/5 forward-referenced are `Purchase Order Configuration` (2, at dep.g1.057/058, targetRef verbatim), `Purchase Order Matching Rules` (1), `Purchase Order Import` (2, correctly deferred as a spec), and `Purchase Order/Request Settings` (correctly re-pointed at Workflows). Four groups extracting fields blind converged on exactly these two pages. All 40 sourceQuotes verify verbatim (the one `grep -F` miss is an elided filename in prose — `preventing-po-transmittal-…-51b11602.md` — not a quote defect), and both byte totals (84,820 / 14,837) match `wc -c` exactly. The Policies collision the brief singled out is correctly settled: the 15,800-byte `policies-the-purchase-order-policy-new-experience-5a1ba7ef.md` contains no click path to a Purchase Order Policy page — every nav string in it points at Policies or Forms and Fields — so routing it to Group 1/5 debt avoided both a duplicate page and losing the richest PO file. The Purchase Order/Request Settings → Workflows resolution is the roster's best work and is fully reproducible, clincher grep included (`select their own approver`: available-invoice-settings-8b3411f0.md = 0, invoice-settings-cace748d.md = 2); it alone prevented two spurious Group 3 pages. WHAT IS WRONG is not the page list but the seed lists, the alias arrays, two verifiable false claims, one silently reconciled navigation contradiction, and one page-binding that is inferential yet presented as attested. Most severe: Page 1's `aliases` array contains `PO Matching Ruleset`, which is a FIELD LABEL on the already-built Policies page (`field.policies.po-matching-ruleset`) — the precise class of mis-binding the deterministic validator can never catch, because it checks quotes against files, not controls against pages. Second: `deliverable_id` is a per-directory constant (41460672 on all 1,209 admin-guides files, 41460673 on all 650 tools-guides), so the brief's own republish-vs-variant heuristic carries zero information; the one place the roster acted on it, declaring `8b356b0e`/`3c7c8336` "same content", is demonstrably wrong — `diff` shows they differ on control type (toggle vs check box) and on a default state ("set by sequence as default") that exists in only one. Richness bytes are ~24% YAML front matter, so per-field economics are overstated across the board. One observation for the orchestrator, not a defect: Shipping Configuration is a genuinely PO-domain admin page with a verified click path, excluded from Group 3 by the brief's list rather than by evidence — so the honest statement is that the PO *matching* config area is two pages while the PO/PR config *domain* is three.

completeness.verdict: The two-page roster SURVIVES an independent corpus sweep — I found no third PO admin page and I tried hard. My own censuses reproduce the roster's: 33 distinct `Invoice > X` targets with exactly two PO-domain; 16 nbsp-separated nav forms with exactly one; 29 `(left menu)` labels with one; 80 `page appears` names with one; a 91-phrase python census of every PO-domain page/window/tool/screen/tab name yielding no new admin surface; and a 194-file PO filename census in which every plausible admin candidate I opened carries no `Administration > Invoice > <new page>` string. The synonym axis is dead (catalog 0, punchout 0, sourcing 0, blanket/standing order 0, encumbrance 0, service entry 0, landed cost 0, requisition 1 incidental). The raw `<table>` sweep returns the briefed 32 files, three PO-domain, none belonging to a Group 3 page — and `grep -c "<table"` is 0 on all 45 seeds, so `rawTableFiles: 0` is verified rather than asserted. My long-catalog sweep over all 350 PO-domain files (corrected for SAP's indented tables, which defeat `^|` greps) finds 50 enumerations of 10+ entries and NOT ONE is a Group 3 seed; every one resolves to Audit Rules, Forms and Fields, Policies, Workflows, Invoice Settings, an import spec, or a guide-cover revision history. All 21 roster sourceQuotes verify at `grep -F -c` >= 1. What the roster loses is at its edges, and two losses are severe. First, eight PO controls are deferred to Groups 1 and 5, both marked complete, and the built graph contains none of them — the root cause is that `page.invoice-settings` holds 13 fields against a 24-row catalog in its own richest source, so deferral there is deletion, not delegation. Second, the roster declared the eleven-page question unverifiable while the answer sat in its own repo: INVOICE-CONFIG-MAP.md records 13 "pages" under the single Workflows menu entry, and the v1 handoff records the lost slice at 24 pages / 145 fields (~6 per page, so 11 x 6 = ~66 PO fields against the roster's own 58 estimate) plus two preserved Group 3 value sets, one of whose labels ("Match Level") has zero corpus hits. Beyond those: an unrecorded 3-vs-4 contradiction on Tolerance across two seed files, six Page-1 seed gaps (three from tools-guides, including the file that actually holds the 6-value Match Status catalog), one Page-2 seed gap that is precisely the cross-directory shape the roster says nearly lost Vendor Search Admin, a fifth click-tree dialog omitted, a debt double-count (5a1ba7ef strictly contains f926eac7, proven paragraph- and table-wise), and a Group 3 seed file that is the only file corpus-wide ending in a bare "x" — a crawl truncation nobody flagged. Keep "do not split 3A/3B": the two seed sets share zero files and neither page owns a long catalog, so the split rule's triggers are absent. But the run is no longer two pages — declare it 2 new pages + 2 patch targets, patch last.
